Since I took the external drive I was using for Time Machine and attached it to my HTPC which was fast running out of storage space, I was in need of another backup solution. I looked at getting a Time Capsule but at the current prices it just didn't make sense. I already have a server that runs a few FreeBSD virtual machines for DNS, DHCP, Samba and rsync; I considered rsync but really wanted something compatible with Time Machine. Enter: Netatalk.

Setup is fairly straight forward. Install netatalk3 from ports or binary package, create a non login user account, assign that user+group permissions to read and write to the directory you're going to export as AFP, start the required services and you're done.

Below is a snippet from /etc/rc.conf for the services required to run netatalk, they will be pulled in automatically if you install the binary package, if you install from ports make sure you enable them in the config before you compile netatalk.

...
dbus_enable="YES"
avahi_daemon_enable="YES"
netatalk_enable="YES"
...

and the configuration file for netatalk that lives in /usr/local/etc/afp.conf

[Global]
mimic model = TimeCapsule
[TimeCapsule]
path = /srv/timecapsule
hosts allow = 192.168.0.130
valid users = timemachine
time machine = yes
vol size limit = 700000

FreeBSD serving a "Time Capsule" backup service to OS X

Heck yeah!! I used this guide to configure mine: http://dae.me/blog/1660/concisest-guide-to-setting-up-time-machine-server-on-ubuntu-server-12-04/

I think there might have been a couple tweaks to the above instructions but it was pretty close.
